'''William Caspar Graustein''' (15 November 1888 – 22 January 1941) was an American mathematician. He graduated magna cum laude from [[Harvard University]] in 1910<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Coolidge|first=J. L.|date=2017-01-27|title=William Caspar Graustein—In memoriam|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183503624|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|language=EN|volume=47|issue=5|pages=343–349|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1941-07433-1|issn=0002-9904|doi-access=free}}</ref> and later became an instructor at Harvard University. In 1921, he married [[Mary Graustein|Mary Curtis Graustein]] (1884&mdash;1972), who was the first American woman to earn a mathematics Ph.D. (1917) from [[Radcliffe College]].<ref name=":0">{{cite book | title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics | isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke | title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics &mdash; The Pre-1940 PhD's | location= | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]], The [[London Mathematical Society]] | series=History of Mathematics | volume=34 | edition=1st | date=2008 }} Mary Florence (Curtis) Graustein biography on p.213-215 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>

He died in an automobile accident, at the age of 52. At the time, Graustein was professor of mathematics and assistant dean at Harvard.<ref name=":0" />

== Bibliography ==

Some of his books and papers are:<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.worldcat.org/search?q=au:Graustein,+William+C.&qt=hot_author|title=Results for 'au:Graustein, William C.' [WorldCat.org]|website=www.worldcat.org|language=en|access-date=2017-01-27}}</ref>

* ''The scientific work of Joseph Lipka''
* ''Applicability with preservation of both curvatures''
* ''Extensions of the [[four-vertex theorem]]''
* ''Introduction to higher geometry''
* ''Differential Geometry'' MacMillan Company 1935. Republished Dover 1966 2006.
